lineup: Hour 1 is all college football Week 5 - the new AP poll, Florida's blowout of Ole Miss, three ranked-on-ranked upsets, West Virginia's loss to Oklahoma State and the trip to Iowa State, then picks on Ohio State-Iowa, Alabama-Mississippi State, Miami-Clemson, Florida-Missouri and Notre Dame-North Carolina. Hour 2 opens with Trent Conner's five-minute fantasy hit, then NFL Week 4 from Thursday night's Browns win through Sunday, the implied team totals and both primetime games.
lines_note: College football lines are FanDuel via FanDuel Research, captured Sept. 30 to Oct. 1; where only another book had a number it is labeled in the segment. NFL lines are DraftKings via ESPN, captured Friday Oct. 2 at 11:19 a.m. ET - one board for all 15 remaining games.
verify: No Friday NFL injury designations were posted when the board was pulled - re-check nfl.com/injuries before air, especially DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Justin Jefferson (ankle), Puka Nacua, Nico Collins and Caleb Williams.
Bears quarterback: Williams is doubtful, Bagent is coming off a concussion, Keenum is reportedly expected to start. Confirm Saturday.
Terry McLaurin being out traces only to a stale 2025 article. Do not say it.
NFL lines moved a point or two off Tuesday's board (Bills, Cardinals, Rams, Packers, 49ers). Re-pull Saturday morning if you plan to read spreads on air.
WVU-Iowa State is -2.5 or -3.5 depending on the book, with the total at 52.5 or 53.5. Call it about a field goal.

Other college spreads differ between books: Alabama -5.5/60.5 vs -6/59.5; Florida -4.5 (FanDuel) vs -5.5 (Oct. 2); Ohio State -14.5 (FanDuel) vs -14 (BetMGM); Miami-Clemson total quoted at 46.5, 47.5 and 49.5.
Washington-USC total is 58.5 on FanDuel and 55.5 at BetMGM - a three-point gap. Re-pull before using it.
Michael Hawkins Jr.'s passing/rushing touchdown split conflicts between two outlets. Use '11 total touchdowns' and his yardage, not the split. His four-game numbers could not be confirmed.
WVU's Coastal Carolina final is reported as both 31-24 and 31-21.
Zac Alley's snap-count quote says 278 while the same article's text says 238. Use the quote as spoken, do not cite the raw number as fact.
Dylan Stewart's suspension is 'indefinite' per AP, 'one game' per ESPN, and one outlet reports him cleared for Missouri. Confirm before describing its length.
Iowa State's defensive national ranks (26th total, 30th scoring) are single-sourced - the official game notes could not be opened.
BYU's starting quarterback was not named in any source found. Do not guess a name on air.
Ohio State's and Iowa's quarterback season numbers are unconfirmed. Skip the stat lines in that game or pull them fresh.
Kirk Ferentz already holds the Big Ten all-time wins record - he passed Woody Hayes in September 2025. He is not approaching it.
Darian Mensah's 88.7 percent completion rate in one source is almost certainly a typo. Use his yards, touchdowns and interceptions only.
Ahmad Hardy's absence involves a gunshot wound. Handle carefully or leave it at 'expected to miss another week.'
Fantasy roster percentages moved all week (Ollie Gordon 1 to 26 percent). Quote them as ranges.

blocks.title: Block 1: Week 4 reset and the new poll

segments.title: The new AP Top 25

items.t: 1 Texas (4-0), 2 Georgia (4-0), 3 Notre Dame (4-0), 4 Miami (4-0), 5 Ohio State (3-1), 6 Indiana (4-0), 7 Alabama (4-0), 8 Florida (4-0), 9 Ole Miss (3-1), 10 BYU (3-0).

11 LSU, 12 Texas Tech, 13 Utah, 14 Iowa, 15 Oregon, 16 Mississippi State, 17 Tennessee, 18 USC, 19 Oklahoma State, 20 Houston, 21 SMU, 22 Boise State, 23 UCLA, 24 Kentucky, 25 Missouri. Poll reflects games through Sept. 26.

items.h: Florida's 13-spot jump is the biggest move in the poll
items.t: Florida goes 21 to 8 after beating Ole Miss. Ole Miss drops five to 9, USC down six to 18, Missouri down six to 25. Mississippi State up eight to 16, Oregon up five to 15, Houston up five to 20. New to the poll: Oklahoma State 19, Boise State 22, UCLA 23, Kentucky 24. Six Big Ten teams ranked.

segments.title: Biggest results

items.t: Jadan Baugh ran for 142 and three touchdowns. Florida outscored Ole Miss 28-7 in the second half and snapped a 12-game losing streak against top-five teams.
Texas survived Knoxville with 262 total yards, 11 penalties for 115 yards and 1.7 yards per carry on 36 attempts.
The Georgia defense forced four turnovers and scored. No. 10 LSU also handled No. 23 Texas A&M 35-6.

items.h: Ohio State 42, Illinois 19 and Alabama 49, South Carolina 18
items.t: Jeremiah Smith went 12 catches, 217 yards, 4 TD for Ohio State. Keelon Russell threw four touchdown passes in the first half for Alabama.

segments.title: The upsets

items.t: Reece Vander Zee caught a 16-yard touchdown with two seconds left and finished 5-66-2. Hank Brown went 21-of-35 for 227 and 2 TD. Iowa won with 285 total yards to Michigan's 429, plus a 99-yard kickoff return by Braeden Jackson and a career-high 12 tackles from Zach Lutmer.
Backup Dylan Raiola threw for 289 and 2 TD after starter Dante Moore went out in the second quarter, leading scoring drives on six of seven possessions.
A 17-point comeback in Happy Valley with two touchdowns inside the final four minutes, the winner a 70-yard pass to tight end Jacob Harris.
Kamario Taylor threw for 360 and 3 TD, the game-winner with 3:57 left. Wake Forest also took down No. 16 Louisville 30-27 when a tying field goal was blocked with 15 seconds left.

segments.title: Oklahoma State 41, West Virginia 24: what went wrong

items.h: 609 yards, and the worst defensive night of the Zac Alley era
items.t: Oklahoma State piled up 609 yards at 9.0 per play - the 10th-highest total in WVU program history and the most ever allowed under defensive coordinator Zac Alley. Drew Mestemaker went 20-of-27 for 389 and 3 TD, with 274 of those yards and two scores coming after halftime. Wyatt Young had 192 receiving, Caleb Hawkins 180 rushing. The Cowboys were 5-for-5 in the red zone.

items.h: WVU moved the ball and still lost by 17
items.t: West Virginia had 466 yards and 334 rushing and won time of possession 31:04 to 28:56. Cam Cook went 29 carries for 193 with a 75-yard run; Michael Hawkins Jr. ran for 102 and three touchdowns but went 10-of-22 passing with an interception. Kamari Wilson had a pick, Ben Cutter eight tackles. WVU recorded zero sacks and allowed four.
Oklahoma State snapped an 18-game Big 12 losing streak dating to November 2023 and has now won six straight in Morgantown. WVU is 3-1, 0-1 in the league.

"We gave up 609 yards. Didn't give our guys a chance." And: "It's the head coach's responsibility to make sure we have a plan that can succeed, and it didn't succeed. So I didn't do a good job of making sure our plan was going to help us succeed." Also: "We never got any pressure." And on Mestemaker: "Good players like that, an NFL quarterback, is going to beat you."

items.h: Alley said the same thing about himself
items.t: "We weren't prepared the way we needed to be. The plan wasn't very good." And: "Giving up 600 yards makes me feel like we weren't ready."

segments.title: Today: West Virginia at Iowa State, Noon ET, TNT

items.h: About a field goal, and the loser is 0-2 in the Big 12
items.t: Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, Noon ET on TNT with a truTV and HBO Max simulcast. Iowa State -2.5, O/U 52.5 on FanDuel; one book had it -3.5 and another had the total at 53.5. Both teams are 0-1 in conference play.

items.h: Iowa State is 2-2 under a first-year head coach
items.t: Beat SEMO 38-10, lost at Iowa 13-16, beat Bowling Green 55-7, lost to Utah 17-31. They are 2-2 against the spread and have gone over the total in each of the last two. Jimmy Rogers is in his first season in Ames after South Dakota State, where he won five conference titles and two FCS championships, with a new offensive coordinator in Tyler Roehl and a new defensive coordinator in Jesse Bobbit.

26th nationally in total defense at 272.5 yards allowed and 30th in scoring at 16.0 a game. Sullivan Schlimgen has 35 tackles, second in the Big 12; Carson Willich has 5 TFL; Isaac Terrell leads with 3 sacks; Beau Goodwin and Beni Ngoyi each have an interception.

items.h: But Rogers volunteered the flaw: 29 missed tackles
items.t: "We had 29 missed tackles, which is really high. Some of those are not finishing. Some of those are over-pursuing."

items.h: The offense is where WVU can win it
items.t: Iowa State averages 345.3 total yards, 14th of 16 in the Big 12, with 164.8 passing - tied 119th nationally - and converts 31.9 percent of third downs, 123rd. Jaylen Raynor, in from Arkansas State, is 50-of-92 for 639 with 5 TD and 3 INT at 54.3 percent, plus 137 rushing and three rushing scores. Aiden Flora leads the rush at 382 yards, 95.5 a game. Omari Hayes has 11 catches for 156, Dominic Overby 7 for 142, Vince Benetti two touchdowns.

items.h: The scheme problem WVU is preparing for
items.t: Alley on Iowa State's personnel churn: "They do a good job of mixing it up. On the season, they've had like 278 snaps. Of that, the same 11 people have been on the field three times." Rodriguez: "This week is a different challenge, because they'll do so many different things formationally on offense."

Iowa State OUT: Caden Crawford, Ka'Mori Moore. Questionable: Jaheim Singletary. West Virginia OUT: Emory Snyder, Armoni Weaver-Bomar, Andre Devine, Darius Wiley. Probable: Nick Taylor, Ashton Woods. One more weekday report Friday night and a final one before kickoff.

All-time it is tied 6-6, but Iowa State has won five of the last six and the last three in Ames. West Virginia is 3-0 at home, 2-2 against the spread and 4-0 to the over. Rogers on WVU's quarterback: "This quarterback, [Michael] Hawkins, is probably one of the fastest players in the country. He's extremely explosive."

segments.title: No. 5 Ohio State at No. 14 Iowa, 3:30 ET, CBS

items.t: FanDuel has it -14.5; BetMGM had Ohio State -14 with the same 45.5 total. Iowa is 4-0 and at Kinnick.

items.h: Jeremiah Smith is the Heisman favorite and the reason to watch
items.t: 33 catches, 617 yards and 7 TD on the season, a national lead in receiving yards, coming off 12 catches for 217 and four touchdowns against Illinois.
Cam Buffington leads the team with 38 tackles, including 15 against Iowa State and 11 against Michigan. Kamari Moulton returned from injury for 13 carries and 44 yards against Michigan.

items.h: The under trends are the strongest angle on the board
items.t: Ohio State is 6-0 to the under as a road team since 2025 and 8-1 to the under as a road favorite since 2024. Iowa is 3-1 against the spread and 3-1 to the under at home, and 6-4 against the spread as a home underdog since 2016.

Iowa has scored zero offensive points across five combined first-quarter drives against Power 4 opponents this season, and ranks 66th in opponent EPA per dropback - the coverage soft spot Smith will attack.
Iowa is currently projected into the playoff field at No. 10. A home win over Ohio State is the validation win Kirk Ferentz has not had.

segments.title: No. 7 Alabama at No. 16 Mississippi State, Noon ET, ABC

items.h: Alabama -5.5, O/U 60.5 - the highest total on the board
items.t: Both teams are 4-0. One book had Alabama -6 with a 59.5 total earlier in the week, so the number has moved.

items.h: The streak nobody in Starkville wants to hear about
items.t: Alabama has won 16 straight in this series. Mississippi State's last win was 2007, and State is chasing a 5-0 start.

items.h: Kamario Taylor is third in the Heisman market
items.t: 1,192 passing yards at roughly 70 percent with 14 TD and 2 INT, plus 37 carries for 185 and a score. He moved up after beating ranked Missouri.

items.h: Keelon Russell is right behind him
items.t: More than 1,100 passing yards and 11 total touchdowns in four games, including 365 and four scores against South Carolina. His Heisman price went from +2200 to +1600.

OUT: defensive backs Jorden Edmonds and Nick Sherman, linebackers Cayden Jones, Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu, and defensive lineman Jeremiah Beaman. Will Sanders probable, Jayvin James questionable. Mississippi State OUT: Trevion Williams, Diesel Moye, Ayden Williams; Isaac Smith questionable.

segments.title: No. 4 Miami at Clemson, 7:30 ET, ABC

items.t: Miami is 4-0, Clemson 3-1, at Memorial Stadium.

items.h: The line movement is the best betting story of the day
items.t: It opened Miami -18.5 and has come down to -16.5, with the total dropping from 51.5 to 47.5. Clemson has drawn 67 to 97 percent of the money on the spread while Miami holds 63 to 79 percent of the tickets - sharp money on the home underdog against public money on the favorite.

items.h: Darian Mensah is second in the Heisman market at +400
items.t: 1,211 passing yards, 14 TD, 0 INT, plus 52 rushing yards and a rushing score.
Freshman Tait Reynolds is making his third career start and has more interceptions, two, than touchdowns, one.

items.h: And Clemson's 3-1 is softer than it reads
items.t: They were beaten badly at LSU in the opener, then beat Georgia Southern, North Carolina and Cal - and the Cal win included a fumble-return touchdown and a 65-yard punt-return touchdown, non-offensive scoring that flatters the offense. Five of Miami's last six games have gone over the total.

segments.title: No. 8 Florida at No. 25 Missouri, 3:30 ET, ABC

items.t: FanDuel had -4.5; an Oct. 2 board had Florida -5.5 with the same total. Florida is 4-0 and 2-0 in the SEC, Missouri 3-1 and 0-1.

items.h: Jadan Baugh is the hottest back in the country
items.t: Four straight games of 100-plus yards and two-plus touchdowns, and 866 rushing yards over his last five at 7.1 a carry. His Heisman odds went from +6000 in Week 3 to +1200.

items.h: Missouri's quarterback has not thrown a pick
items.t: Austin Simmons has 11 touchdowns and zero interceptions, and went 23-of-39 for 295 and three scores against Mississippi State. Cayden Lee had 11 catches for 156 and two touchdowns in that game. Running back Ahmad Hardy is expected to miss another week.

Missouri is 1-3 against the spread, 0-2 at home, and 0-5-1 against the spread versus ranked opponents since last season. Florida is 3-1 against the spread and 1-0 on the road, but 4-7 as a road favorite since 2021. This is also a classic letdown spot a week after Florida hung 52 on Ole Miss.
Florida's Jayden Woods leads the team with 4.5 sacks and has at least half a sack in three straight. Missouri's Daeden Hopkins has 6 sacks, 6.5 TFL and two forced fumbles.

segments.title: No. 3 Notre Dame at North Carolina, Noon ET, ESPN - and the hot seat

items.h: Notre Dame -21.5, O/U 47.5, and a series record that is barely believable
items.t: Notre Dame leads this series 21-1 all time. The last meeting was 2022, a 45-32 Irish win.

items.h: Belichick, year two, and a buyout number
items.t: North Carolina opened with a 15-10 win over TCU in Ireland and beat ETSU 35-3, then lost at Clemson 28-20 on a fourth-quarter collapse. Bill Belichick appears on this week's hot-seat list with a $10-12 million buyout and staff resignations under investigation.

Billy Edwards Jr. is 44-of-78 for 611 with 3 TD and 1 INT and has taken seven sacks. North Carolina ranks 91st in EPA per play, 108th in passing success rate and 103rd in EPA per pass, and has scored 20 or fewer in both Power 4 games.

items.h: Notre Dame is rolling on both sides
items.t: CJ Carr is completing better than 70 percent with 9 TD and 1 INT, including 237 and three scores against Purdue, and is sixth in Heisman odds. Chris Ash's defense allows 199 yards a game and held Purdue to 218. Notre Dame has covered in three of four and averages better than 40 points. Safety Luke Talich is expected back. Even the kicking is a gap: Spencer Porath is 5-of-6 with a 52-yard long, Aeron Burrell 4-of-7 with a 33-yard long.

items.h: Three hot-seat coaches host games today
items.t: Belichick against Notre Dame, Lincoln Riley against Washington with roughly a $60 million buyout, and Sonny Dykes against BYU at about $25 million. Also on the list: Shane Beamer, Mike Locksley at 2-15 in his last 17 Big Ten games, and Mike Norvell at a $45-50 million buyout with his athletic director already fired.

segments.title: Rest of the board, the Heisman and the bracket

items.h: Michigan at Minnesota, Noon FOX - Michigan -5.5, O/U 43.5
items.t: The Little Brown Jug, and Michigan is going for a sixth straight year holding it. Minnesota has won it only four times since 1968 and P.J. Fleck is 0-4 with the Jug on the line. Michigan has covered in nine of the last 12 meetings and the under is 7-1 in Minnesota's last eight home games. Watch Bryce Underwood's 5.4 percent turnover-worthy play rate against a Minnesota defense sixth nationally in havoc rate.

items.h: Washington at No. 18 USC, 7:30 NBC - USC -9.5
items.t: Washington has won three straight in this series and four of the last five, including three of four at the Coliseum. Demond Williams Jr. took seven sacks against Minnesota and said "a lot of times I was holding the ball too long. I just feel like it falls on me." Washington ran for 50 yards on 27 attempts in that game. USC is coming off a 41-27 home loss to Oregon with a long injury list: out are Corey Simms, Kendarius Reddick and Kilian O'Connor, with Jahkeem Stewart, Trent Mosley and Mark Bowman questionable.

items.h: No. 10 BYU at TCU, 7:00 ESPN - BYU -6.5, O/U 47.5
items.t: Both kickers are out - BYU's Brody Laga and TCU's Kyle Lemmermann. BYU is off a bye at 3-0; TCU is 2-2 and has not beaten a power-conference opponent, with losses to North Carolina and UCF. LJ Martin is averaging 7.8 yards a carry on 42 touches for BYU. More than 90 percent of the bets are on BYU and the line has not moved.

Auburn at No. 17 Tennessee 3:30 ESPN, Tennessee -7.5, O/U 54.5. South Carolina at No. 24 Kentucky 4:15 SECN. Rutgers at No. 6 Indiana 8:00 BTN, Indiana -24.5. Vanderbilt at No. 2 Georgia 12:45 SECN, Georgia -24.5. UCF at No. 20 Houston Noon ESPN2. No. 1 Texas and Oregon are both on bye; Red River is Oct. 10 at the Cotton Bowl.

DraftKings: Jeremiah Smith +245, Darian Mensah +400, Kamario Taylor +480, Trinidad Chambliss +1150 after falling from +310, Jadan Baugh +1200, CJ Carr +1300, Keelon Russell +1700. Smith holds the most wagers and the most money at BetMGM. Radio stat: only one wide receiver has won the Heisman since 1992.

Current bracket: 1 Texas, 2 Ohio State, 3 Miami, 4 Georgia, 5 Notre Dame, 6 Indiana, 7 Alabama, 8 Florida, 9 Texas Tech, 10 Iowa, 11 Ole Miss, 12 Boise State. Just outside: LSU, BYU, Oregon, Utah, Mississippi State - and the SEC is positioned to send five or more.

hours.title: Hour 2
hours.subtitle: Trent Conner's fantasy five at 9:00, then NFL Week 4 (9:05-10:00)

segments.title: SEGMENT: Trent's fantasy five

items.h: The news that changed everyone's week
items.t: De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL. Ollie Gordon II is the must-add - he took all the Miami back work for 17-41-1 and caught all three of his targets, and he is rostered anywhere from 1 to 26 percent depending on the site.

Tyler Shough (NO vs ATL) leads the league in attempts and completions and has cleared 22 points every week. Josh Downs (IND vs WAS) faces the defense allowing the most to receivers. Tetairoa McMillan (CAR vs DET) has 176 yards on 18 targets the last two weeks. Dalton Schultz (HOU vs DAL) is second among tight ends in targets.

Justin Herbert at Seattle has not hit 14 points in a game and sits bottom-eight in passer rating, completion percentage and EPA per dropback. Jameson Williams at Carolina is at 1.2 yards per route run against the defense allowing the fewest points to receivers. Kyle Pitts has two catches for 20 yards all season.

items.h: Stash moves and streamers in one breath
items.t: Dalton Kincaid and Denzel Boston have graduated off the stash list - start them both. Drop Kaelon Black and Rashod Bateman. Hold Tank Dell if you have an IR slot, he is listed eligible to return Week 5. Streamers: Darren Waller at tight end, Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, and Green Bay's defense against an undrafted rookie's first career start.

segments.title: Thursday night: Browns 27, Steelers 24

items.t: Andre Szmyt won it after Deshaun Watson went 4-of-5 for 46 yards on the drive, and Grant Delpit intercepted Aaron Rodgers on the final play. Cleveland led 21-7 late in the first half before Rodgers tied it with a touchdown to Pat Freiermuth inside two minutes.

Watson 24-of-33, 268, 1 TD, 1 INT - his second straight game-winning drive after Carolina. Rodgers 22-of-40, 299, 3 TD, 2 INT, sacked five times. Jaylen Warren 17-93, DK Metcalf 5-115, Quinshon Judkins 17-53 and a touchdown, Denzel Boston 4-89 with a 60-yarder. Cleveland had a season-high five sacks, two interceptions and 372 net yards.

items.h: Browns 3-1 for the first time since 2021
items.t: Pittsburgh drops to 2-2.

Steelers: Derrick Harmon carted off with a foot injury and in a boot afterward, Jamel Dean re-aggravated an ankle and was ruled out, Roman Wilson hurt late. Browns: Mason Graham left with a knee injury. No diagnoses released on any of them.

segments.title: Week 3 rewind and the Week 4 board

items.t: Case Keenum, in for the injured Caleb Williams, went 24-of-34 for 247 and 2 TD. Jalen Hurts 16-of-25, 153, no touchdowns, one pick; Saquon Barkley 15-82; Kalif Raymond 6-90-1.
Washington knocked off the defending champs. Marcus Mariota 19-of-31, 183, 3 TD. Sam Darnold threw for 379 and four scores in the loss, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 10-128-2.
Lamar Jackson 15-of-20 for 186 and 2 TD, Derrick Henry 26-89 with two scores, Dak Prescott 25-of-40 for 276, CeeDee Lamb 7-112.

Vegas is 3-0 under first-year coach Klint Kubiak - Kirk Cousins 22-of-33, 248, 3 TD and Brock Bowers 10-116-1. San Francisco is also 3-0 behind Brock Purdy 15-of-27, 297, 4 TD, George Kittle 6-82-2 and 17 tackles from Fred Warner.

Steelers 30 Bengals 27 with Rodgers at 292 and three scores and Jaylen Warren 17-127. Broncos 30 Rams 26 on Sunday night, Stafford 390 and Davante Adams 7-137. Bills 24 Chargers 16 despite five Buffalo turnovers and 10 penalties, James Cook 24-154-1. Jaguars 35 Patriots 6 with two Drake Maye interceptions.
Unbeaten at 3-0: Chiefs, Bills, Raiders, Vikings, 49ers. Winless at 0-3: Dolphins, Chargers, Titans, Texans, Buccaneers. Browns 3-1.

16 games, no byes, 15 left after Thursday. DraftKings via ESPN, captured Friday Oct. 2 at 11:19 a.m. ET. Highest total Jaguars-Bengals 51.5; lowest Packers-Buccaneers and Dolphins-Vikings 38.5; biggest spread Ravens -11.5.

segments.title: Early window

items.h: Colts vs Commanders in London, 9:30 a.m. ET, NFL Network - IND -3.5, O/U 48.5
items.t: Jayden Daniels is out with the elbow and Marcus Mariota starts. Washington is also without Sam Cosmi (concussion) and Nick Cross, with Frankie Luvu questionable. Keenan Allen is questionable with a groin for Indy and Alec Pierce is on IR.

items.h: Patriots at Bills, 1:00 ET, CBS - BUF -7, O/U 48.5
items.t: A.J. Brown is on IR for New England into mid-October. Buffalo has Christian Benford (toe), Keon Coleman (ankle), DJ Moore (shoulder) and Damar Hamlin (ribs) all questionable.

items.h: Cowboys at Texans, 1:00 ET, FOX - HOU -3, O/U 48.5
items.t: Nico Collins is questionable but back at practice after missing two games. Dallas is without Tyler Smith, Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke, with DeMarvion Overshown questionable.

items.h: Jets at Bears, 1:00 ET, FOX - CHI -3.5, O/U 42.5
items.t: Caleb Williams is doubtful with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Tyson Bagent is coming off a concussion, and Case Keenum is reportedly expected to start again. Breece Hall is out for the Jets with a quad.

items.h: Titans at Ravens, 1:00 ET, CBS - BAL -11.5, O/U 42.5
items.t: The biggest spread on the board. Lamar Jackson practiced fully after the back issue. Ethan Pocic is out, Ronnie Stanley and Trey Hendrickson questionable.

segments.title: Late window and quick hits

items.h: Dolphins at Vikings, 4:05 ET, FOX - MIN -10.5, O/U 38.5
items.t: De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL. Justin Jefferson is questionable with an ankle and did not practice, described as day-to-day.

items.h: Broncos at 49ers, 4:25 ET, CBS - SF -3, O/U 47.5
items.t: Nick Bosa is out for weeks with a calf and knee issue, Mykel Williams is out for the year, and Trent Williams and Mike Evans are questionable.

items.h: Rams at Eagles, 1:00 ET, FOX - LAR -3.5, O/U 42.5
items.t: DeVonta Smith is doubtful with a hamstring and Dallas Goedert is doubtful with the knee. Puka Nacua is expected back for the Rams.

items.h: Jaguars at Bengals, Chiefs at Raiders, Chargers at Seahawks
items.t: Cincinnati -2.5, O/U 51.5 - the top total of the week. Kansas City -4.5, O/U 47.5 at 4:25. Seattle -7, O/U 42.5 at 4:05.

Cardinals at Giants, Arizona -2.5, O/U 44.5, with Jameis Winston starting for New York and Jaxson Dart on IR. Packers at Buccaneers, Green Bay -3.5, O/U 38.5, with Baker Mayfield out at least three weeks on a dislocated thumb and undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels making his first career start.

segments.title: Where the number says the value is

items.t: Implied team totals off the same DraftKings board, captured Friday Oct. 2 at 11:19 a.m. ET. Favorite is (total plus spread) divided by two; underdog is (total minus spread) divided by two.

Cincinnati and Detroit are the offenses Vegas likes most without a big spread, and the Bengals-Jaguars 51.5 is the week's top total. Baltimore's 27.0 is built entirely off the 11.5-point spread rather than the total - that is a Jackson-and-Henry game, not a shootout. Miami at 14.0 is a full fade. And Philadelphia at 19.5 as a home underdog is the talking point of the week.

segments.title: SNF: Lions at Panthers, 8:20 ET, NBC

items.h: Detroit -3.5, O/U 50.5 - the highest total in primetime
items.t: Carolina put Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) on IR and has Xavier Legette doubtful. D.J. Reed is questionable for Detroit.

segments.title: MNF: Falcons at Saints, 8:15 ET, ESPN

items.t: The Saints are without Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring), Jordyn Tyson and Kelvin Banks Jr., all on IR. Atlanta has Divine Deablo and Samson Ebukam questionable with hamstrings.

segments.title: Lock of the week and close

items.h: One play, one sentence from each panelist
items.t: Go around the table for a lock of the week.
Reset the primetime slate - Lions at Panthers Sunday night, Falcons at Saints Monday night - then tease next week: Red River on Oct. 10 and Tank Dell's return window.
